review_notes:
I read all of SparseGeometry.lean. Most of it is empty namespace and section scaffolding. The real content is `sites`, `origin`, `translate` and their lemmas. The only simp attribute in the file is `@[simp] mem_sites`. It unfolds membership in the `Finset.Icc ×ˢ Finset.Icc` box to a four-way conjunction of linear inequalities. That is a sensible normal form. The other `mem_sites` lemmas in the repo (ProductGraph, CantorProjective) are in different namespaces, and I found no sign of a rule conflict or rewrite cycle. I checked the downstream uses of the unannotated lemmas:
- `mem_enlarged` is only ever applied as `.mp` or `.mpr` (SparseWitnessModel.lean).
- `translate_dist` is used in a single `rw` (SparseGeodesic.lean `pathEdges_card`).
- `translate_adj` and `translate_mem` are applied directly as terms.
- `card_sites` is passed explicitly in one `simp only` list (SparseWitnessModel.lean `short_entropy`).
None of these is a use where a missing simp attribute causes a concrete problem, so I did not recommend annotating them. I did not run Lean, so I could not check how simp behaves on `mem_sites`. I also did not check the body proofs of `face_neighbor_sites` (`norm_num [...]`) or `translate_surj` (`simp [translate,y]`) for fragility.
